title: The Logic of Risk Taking
coreMove: Refuse any risk whose downside can end future participation, no matter how attractive the upside looks.
sourcePressure: Risk must be judged through ruin, leverage, and nonlinear downside rather than exciting upside or bravery stories.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making the ending motivational risk-taking advice instead of ruin-sensitive judgment.

sourceAnchors.name: The Logic of Risk Taking
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar supports closing on ruin-sensitive risk, leverage, nonlinear downside, and survival logic.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The final test is blunt: if a bad outcome removes you from the game, the upside story is not the main fact.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: founder offered leveraged growth financing with personal guarantees
exampleSpecs.audience: operator distinguishing bold upside from ruin exposure
exampleSpecs.stakes: one bad quarter could end the company and personal solvency

exampleSpecs.domain: mountain guide deciding whether to continue in unstable weather for a summit bonus
exampleSpecs.audience: guide weighing reversible discomfort against irreversible loss
exampleSpecs.stakes: clients may confuse courage with ruin blindness

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital pharmacy considering a cheaper single supplier for critical medication
exampleSpecs.stakes: short-term savings could become patient harm if supply fails

exampleSpecs.domain: retiree tempted into high-yield private credit after years of low returns
exampleSpecs.audience: advisor applying ruin sensitivity to attractive yield
exampleSpecs.stakes: income upside cannot compensate for principal loss that ends independence

exampleSpecs.domain: city approving one coastal road design with no retreat option

exampleSpecs.stakes: a single flood could remove the only route, not just damage it

exampleSpecs.firstImage: salt crust on a road survey stake

exampleSpecs.domain: chef deciding whether to serve a risky preservation experiment at a paid dinner
exampleSpecs.audience: chef distinguishing small trial from irreversible reputation and health loss
exampleSpecs.stakes: one contamination event ends trust beyond the evening's profit
